headline: A BUYER PUT 355 COMANCHE AT THE TOP OF THEIR LIST LAST NIGHT — the agent who called you from inside the house filed her form at 11:24 PM saying her buyers really like it and it's their #1, and she left both price fields blank, which makes five straight reads since the cut where nobody argued the number. · DO: book the 225 Willow Point photographer — the shoot is TOMORROW · WATCH: Make credits pause the whole automation layer around Thursday.

notes: ✅ THE MORNING LETTER FIRED ON TIME — and that closes the three-day slip this board led with yesterday. The Daily sent at 6:45 this morning, on its own schedule, with no catch-up stack behind it; the gap to the previous routine was eighteen minutes. For context on how bad it had gotten: Friday's edition did not arrive until 8:24 Saturday morning, twenty-six hours late, and Saturday produced no letter at all. Today it simply ran. The build queued to detect exactly this failure is still unshipped, but it is no longer the top of the build list, because the thing it watches is working again.

✅ ROUGHLY TWENTY-FIVE ON-TIME PASSES SINCE YESTERDAY MORNING, NO DARK WINDOW, NOTHING BLOCKED — the overnight was genuinely quiet in the way a healthy fleet is quiet: the lead lane correctly did nothing on a Sunday no-touch, the sweeps ran every twenty to thirty minutes through 9 PM and picked back up at 6:12 this morning, and the evening close sent on schedule. Two brand-new seller leads arrived after 7 PM and both got a first touch inside five minutes.

🛑 ONE REAL COUNTDOWN, AND IT IS THE ONLY THING ON THIS BOARD WITH A HARD DATE — the automation platform is 75% through its credit cycle and every scenario on it pauses when the meter runs out, projected around Thursday, with the cycle not renewing until roughly the 30th. That is a nine-to-ten day window in which the instant-lead alert and the send path for these very briefings both stop. ⚠️ Also still open and unchanged: voicemail forwarding to the secondary company address has failed on every attempt since 8/12 — seventeen bounce threads, no exceptions. Voicemails still land in the primary inbox, which is why nothing has been lost.

callBlock.who: Amy G. of Ethos International — her buyers put 355 Comanche TOP OF THEIR LIST last night
callBlock.why: 🔥 THE HOTTEST THING TO LAND ON THIS BOARD IN DAYS, AND IT ARRIVED AT 11:24 LAST NIGHT. She answered interested — YES, and wrote in her own words that her buyers have just started looking, really like the property, and have put it at the top of their list. ⭐ WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM THE OTHER YESES ON THIS HOUSE: she is the same agent who phoned you from inside the home mid-showing yesterday afternoon, and you already answered half of what she asked by text. The channel is open and warm — this is a returned call, not a cold approach. ⚠️ THE HALF YOU DID NOT ANSWER IS THE PROBLEM: she reported the basement lights would not come on, and it is still open. Buyers who have 'just started looking' will tour more houses this week, and the last thing they saw in yours was a dark basement. ⭐ She also left BOTH price fields blank and scored staging a 3 — she is the only agent to score staging since the cut, so ask her what she would change.

callBlock.who: Robert C. — the 198 Rena buyer, now roughly seventy hours unreturned
callBlock.why: 🔥 STILL THE OLDEST LIVE BUYER SIGNAL ON THE BOARD, AND IT HAS NOW RUN THREE FULL DAYS. He phoned you directly Thursday morning asking for photos of the workshop and the garage — not a form, a person who studied the listing closely enough to know what was missing from it. ⭐ YOUR OWN NOTE PUT A LAST NAME TO HIM AND ESCALATED WHAT HE WANTS: this stopped being a photo request and became a showing request. ⏰ THE TIMING JUST GOT SHARPER — the listing agreement reinstates TOMORROW, so a buyer asking to walk through arrives in the same week the sellers decide whether to keep going. On a listing that produced one written offer all summer, an unrepresented buyer asking to see it is the cheapest at-bat you own. ⚠️ Stated honestly: if you called him from the truck it would not show here.

callBlock.who: Claire C. — buyer from Saturday, and the phone is the ONLY way to reach her
callBlock.why: 🆕 SHE REGISTERED SATURDAY EARLY AFTERNOON and the machine handled her end to end in four minutes: ownership verified, first touch sent — and it hard-bounced one second later. ⚠️ HER EMAIL IS AN APPLE PRIVATE-RELAY ADDRESS, the third time this exact pattern has been confirmed on this desk. There is no email path to her at all, now or ever. ⭐ THAT MAKES THIS A DIFFERENT KIND OF TASK FROM THE REST OF THE LIST — every other name here can be worked two ways. This one cannot, and she is now roughly a day and a half old, which is well past the window where speed-to-lead is worth anything.

callBlock.who: Anonymous call-in lead — a real person phoned the CRM Friday and nobody has called back
callBlock.why: ☎️ A HUMAN DIALLED YOUR NUMBER FRIDAY AFTERNOON. The record carries no name and no email — the phone is the only channel that exists, so this one genuinely cannot be worked any other way. ⚠️ THE ALERT SAT UNREAD FROM FRIDAY EVENING UNTIL SATURDAY MORNING'S SWEEP FOUND IT, and that is the whole cost here: an inbound phone call is the highest-intent lead type on the board and this one is now two days cold. ⭐ Ownership is verified as yours at the strong rung, so there is no question about whether it is your lead to work.

callBlock.who: Thomas D. — he said YES on Friday, and the document he asked for now exists
callBlock.why: ✅ THIS IS THE ONE THAT UNBLOCKED ITSELF. He replied "Yes" Friday morning and asked for the White Tail Run lot layout and the per-acre number. 🆕 THE 19-LOT PLAT WAS LOCATED LATER THE SAME MORNING — the exact deliverable his open chip had been waiting on. ⭐ SO THE CALL IS NO LONGER A HOLDING REPLY, IT IS A DELIVERY, which is a completely different conversation to have. 🔥 He is one of six names off the 19-lot ad, and that ad remains the only advertising in the portfolio producing anything at all. ⏰ Two days have now passed since he answered — the gap between 'he said yes' and 'nobody called' is where this one dies.

callBlock.who: Gloria F. — the tenant answer is now twenty-three days owed
callBlock.why: 🔴 THE LONGEST-RUNNING BROKEN PROMISE ON THE BOARD. She waited nineteen days without complaining, then escalated three times in twenty-seven minutes on Wednesday night — two voicemails and a text. ✅ THE EMERGENCY HALF RESOLVED WITHOUT YOU: power is back on at the property and the tenant paid his balance, both confirmed. ⭐ THAT MAKES THE CALL EASIER, NOT UNNECESSARY — what she actually asked is still unanswered: is the tenant out, because he owes another month if he is not. ⭐ YOU DO NOT NEED THE ANSWER TO MAKE THE CALL, and waiting for one is exactly what turned six days into twenty-three.

callBlock.who: Chesley C. — five days unreturned, mid-transaction, on the cleanest deal you have
callBlock.why: ⚠️ THE ODD PART IS WHO THIS IS — not a cold lead but the seller on the file this board calls the cleanest on the board, with the inspection and the appraisal both already spent and the close receipted for 8/28. ⭐ A CLIENT MID-TRANSACTION WHO CALLS AND GETS NOTHING BACK IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE SILENCE YOU CAN BUY, because it costs the referral rather than the closing. ⚠️ There is live business on the same call: the payoff was reported as "forgotten" rather than ordered, and the appraised value still has not come back at day ten. Both are one phone call, not two.

callBlock.who: Angela B. and Cassie C. — the two agents who called Comanche too high and still have not been told it came down
callBlock.why: 🔴 BOTH CHIPS ARE NOW EIGHT DAYS OVERDUE AND LAST NIGHT MADE THE CASE STRONGER. Cassie's buyer toured 7/25, wrote the offer and called the old ask too high; Angela's buyer toured 8/2, said interested YES and called the same old ask too high. Neither knows the price moved. 🆕 A THIRD AGENT FILED A YES LAST NIGHT AND DID NOT ARGUE THE NUMBER — that is now five consecutive reads since the cut where nobody has written down a different price. ⭐ The pricing question on this house is settled; what is not settled is that two agents with interested buyers are still working off a dead number. ⛔ Quote the current list price only, and call rather than email — co-op agents are the red lane under your own rule.

listings.status: 🔴 Coming to market $185K — THE SHOOT IS TOMORROW AND NO PHOTOGRAPHER IS BOOKED
listings.note: 🔴 THIS IS THE ONE ITEM ON THE WHOLE BOARD WITH A DEADLINE THAT ARRIVES BEFORE YOU READ THIS AGAIN. The sellers asked in writing on 8/12 for a MONDAY photo shoot. It is now Sunday morning, tomorrow's calendar holds a 2:30 brokerage call and a 3:00 team call and no shoot, and no photographer has been booked. Four days have passed since they asked. ⭐ THIS IS ALSO THE CHEAPEST PROBLEM ON THE BOARD TO SOLVE — it is one phone call this morning, and Sunday is not too late to make it. ✅ EVERYTHING ELSE ON THIS FILE WENT RIGHT: both sellers executed all seven documents Friday morning, she at 11:41 and he at 11:49, on three separate receipts, and the milestone engine fired this address for the first time in its life. ⚠️ Worth remembering because it was almost an alarm: Friday's morning sweep flagged the agreement as maybe-unsigned six minutes into her signing session. A false positive by minutes, logged as one rather than quietly dropped. ⚠️ The $185,000 price is your own ruling and is quotable, but it still has no primary MLS source behind it. ⭐ And remember what this relationship actually is: she came in unprompted off a listing alert saying they were very interested in a property AND about ready to list their own. This is the LIST half of a two-sided deal, and the BUY half has never been worked.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $295K — a buyer put it TOP OF THEIR LIST last night, and the price question is now settled
listings.note: 🔥 THE BEST NEWS ON THE BOARD THIS MORNING. Amy G. of Ethos International filed her feedback at 11:24 last night off Saturday's 1:00 PM tour: interested — YES, and in her own words her buyers have just started looking, really like the property, and have put it at the top of their list. ⭐ SHE IS THE SAME AGENT WHO PHONED YOU FROM INSIDE THE HOUSE mid-showing, which means the channel is already warm and open — this is a returned call, not a cold approach. ✅ THE PRICING QUESTION ON THIS HOUSE IS NOW ANSWERED AS FIRMLY AS FEEDBACK CAN ANSWER IT: she left BOTH price fields blank, and that makes FIVE consecutive reads since the 8/5 cut where nobody has argued the number. Every read that ever said TOO HIGH was filed while the ask was $299,000. A $4,000 experiment that worked — do not reopen price with this seller. 🔴 THE LIVE ITEM IS THE BASEMENT LIGHTS. She reported on the phone that they would not turn on, you answered the garage half by text at 4:16 and that half is closed, and this half is still open with its own chip. Buyers who have 'just started looking' tour more houses this week — the last thing they saw here was a dark basement. ⭐ She scored staging a 3 and is the ONLY agent to score staging since the cut, so she is worth asking what she would change. 🔴 Two co-op agents who expressed buyer interest still do not know the price moved — both chips overdue since 8/8. ⛔ Quote $295,000 only. ⛔ Call, don't email. ⚠️ One older thread is still unanswered: the 8/10 agent asked in writing whether the ceiling stains came from a previous leak.

listings.status: ⚖️ Active $450K — the agreement reinstates TOMORROW, and the buyer is still unreturned
listings.note: ⏰ THE DATE IS FINALLY SETTLED AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THIS BOARD CARRIED FOR THREE DAYS. Three independent sources now read 8/17 — the CRM crawl, the Ops Board reminder, and the chip that first caught the conflict — so the agreement reinstates TOMORROW, not last Friday. This board printed 8/14 twice and was wrong both times; the correction is logged rather than quietly swapped. ⚠️ AND IT IS A REINSTATEMENT, NOT AN EXTENSION — that came from Don himself Saturday morning, along with the fact that Mrs Ann had not yet been asked as of that reply. 🔴 THE LIVE HUMAN ITEM IS STILL THE ONE THAT MATTERS: Robert C. phoned Thursday morning about the workshop and garage, your own note escalated him from photos to a showing, and he is now roughly seventy hours unreturned with zero outbound on any channel this desk can read. ⭐ THE PRICING PICTURE IS UNCHANGED AND NOTHING HAS MOVED IT: day 91, no price change since May, exactly one written offer all summer, the 8/11 full-price showing this board carried for two days NEVER HAPPENED by the agent's own admission, and Friday's tour ran and produced total silence. ⭐ Both feedback forms this house has ever produced left every price field blank — the objections were the upstairs bathroom and a compartmentalized interior. Nobody who walked it has ever named a different number. ⚠️ Quote $450,000 only until the sellers rule.

listings.status: ✅ Under contract $899K — closes THURSDAY, and it is the quietest high-risk file you have
listings.note: ⏰ FOUR DAYS OUT AND THIS IS THE NEAREST CLOSING ON THE BOARD. ✅ What is verified and good: the appraisal is complete and clean on the lender's own words, the repair addendum is fully executed, the septic inspection ran 8/4, and the closing invite matches the stored state on the engine's own check. ⭐ CLOSING IS THURSDAY 8/20 AT 3:00 PM at the closing attorney's office. 🆕 THE BROKERAGE ISSUED THE COMMISSION DOCUMENT SATURDAY MORNING — the step three separate reminders had been chasing. That starts the payment clock on the largest number closing this month. ⚠️ THE HONEST WORRY IS THE SILENCE, NOT A PROBLEM — this desk has called it the quietest high-risk file in the book all week and nothing has come in since. Four days out with no traffic is worth one confirmation call to the attorney rather than an assumption. ⛔ The old 8/14 close date is retired — do not re-print it anywhere. ⭐ One thing worth having ready: a closing this size is the strongest referral moment you will get this month, and the review-ask on the last funded closing is still sitting untouched at twenty-six days.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $550K — two showings in one Saturday, and still not one word back
listings.note: 🆕 TWO SEPARATE AGENTS WALKED THIS HOUSE ON SATURDAY, SIX HOURS APART — one at 11:10 in the morning and one at 4:00 in the afternoon, taking the all-time counter from 41 to 42 in a single day. ✅ THE SOURCE PROBLEM THIS BOARD FLAGGED FOR TWO DAYS IS CLOSED: both notices print the list price at $550,000. Every prior notice on file printed $559,000 because they all predated the cut, so the price was one source seen repeatedly. It is now confirmed independently and it is quotable. ⭐ THE TIMING IS THE POINT — the cut went live 8/13 and produced two tours inside forty-eight hours on a house whose last read called it too high. That is the market answering the question directly. 🔴 NEITHER TOUR HAS FILED FEEDBACK, AND THE 8/10 TOUR BEFORE THEM NEVER DID EITHER — three showings deep with nothing returned, which is the single biggest information gap on the board. 🔴 THE ITEM THIS BOARD HAS CARRIED UNACTIONED FOR THREE WEEKS IS STILL THE ONE THAT WOULD MOVE THE NEEDLE: the 7/23 read said dirty plus GLITCHING ELECTRICAL, and the 8/4 read scored staging 2 of 5, the lowest this listing has ever recorded, against a 4 three weeks earlier from an agent who called the price JUST RIGHT. The house did not get more expensive between those visits — it got less presentable. ⚠️ And the cut itself still has not been published: the live 8/10 social post carries $559,000 four days after the price moved.

listings.status: 🎉 Under contract $390,000 — the response WENT OUT, and the draft still sitting in the folder is a duplicate
listings.note: ✅ CORRECTION WORTH READING, BECAUSE THIS BOARD HAD IT WRONG YESTERDAY. The inspection-response letter to the sellers was NOT sitting unsent — you sent it yourself Saturday morning at 9:54. The document still sitting in the drafts folder is a DUPLICATE created six minutes later, and it is flagged for deletion rather than aging as pending follow-up. Two separate reads called it 'unsent for 24 hours'; both were reading the copy, not the original. ⭐ THE SHAPE OF THE ASK IS THE STORY AND IT IS GOOD NEWS: they inspected seventy-one items, flagged sixty-eight at some level, and then asked for exactly three. That is a reasonable buyer. ⭐ THE RECOMMENDATION YOU SENT IS TWO YESES AND A HOLD — agree to the basement leak and to a scoped HVAC service, and on the roof do not say no, say give us a few days and our own licensed roofer's report. The inspector wrote in the same section that he cannot determine the roof's age or remaining life, which is the report itself saying the roof question is unanswered. ⚠️ TWO THINGS BEFORE FIGHTING THE ROOF: this is FHA, so the appraiser can raise it independently, and the concession room left under the FHA cap is small, so this gets solved with work rather than a check. ✅ The sellers have acknowledged the roof-holdback approach. ⭐ Closing 10/23 — roughly ten weeks, which is a luxury most files do not get.

listings.status: ✅ Under contract — both gates cleared, close 8/28, and the seller is still waiting on a call
listings.note: ✅ STILL THE CLEANEST FILE ON YOUR BOARD ON PAPER. Both gates are behind you: the inspection ran 8/5 at noon and the appraisal 8/7 at 9:00 AM, both on primary notices, and the closing invite matches the stored state. ⭐ AN INSPECTION AND AN APPRAISAL BOTH SPENT IS THE STRONGEST POSITION ANY DEAL ON THIS BOARD OCCUPIES. 🔴 AND YET THE SELLER HAS BEEN WAITING ON A RETURNED CALL SINCE TUESDAY — five days now, mid-transaction, on the deal with the least to worry about. That is the row on this file that needs you. ⚠️ THE PAYOFF WEAKENED RATHER THAN FIRMED: it was reported as "forgotten" rather than ordered, and forgotten is not ordered, ordered is not received by title. ⚠️ The appraised value still has not come back — day ten, reported as a single-source observation rather than an alarm, and worth one call to the lender. ⚠️ One number remains unruled and it is worth real money on an otherwise settled deal: the buyer's agent asked for a specific co-op commission and nobody has ever answered.

listings.status: 🎉 Under contract $162K — inspection held, both price reads validated the number
listings.note: ✅ THE FIRST GATE IS BEHIND YOU — inspection confirmed and held 8/13 at 10:00 AM; MLS reads CONTINGENT. ✅ THE PAPERWORK ITEM IS CLOSED, NOT PENDING: the contract went out with all signatures, the contract-to-close packet reached title 8/12, and the closing attorney confirmed receipt. ⚠️ ONE THREAD THAT IS NOT CLOSED: the executed contract has been with your operations manager since Tuesday and four days have passed without a status back. On a file this clean that is a process gap rather than a deal risk, but it is the kind that becomes a deal risk quietly. ⭐ TWO INDEPENDENT READS NOW VALIDATE THIS PRICE — the agent who wrote the offer called it JUST RIGHT, and a late form off the 8/7 tour said interested No but PRICED JUST RIGHT with a staging 3 of 5. That is the kind of evidence that matters if anything wobbles before 9/14. ⭐ THE BACKSTORY IS WORTH KEEPING ON THE RECORD: the buyer's agent said her client really liked it but needed to save more for a down payment, and this desk argued for two weeks against reading that as a price signal — she had written JUST RIGHT on the same form. She wrote. Offer to acceptance in twenty-eight minutes. Patience was the right call. ⭐ Closing 9/14.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $184K — a 'VERY interested' buyer is now eight days unworked
listings.note: 🔥 THE LISTING THIS BOARD ONCE CALLED INVISIBLE PRODUCED THREE TOURS IN A SINGLE SATURDAY, all three forms filed within ninety minutes of each other on 8/8. One answered the interest question with the single word "Very" and left every other field blank — which is exactly why it needs a phone call: the enthusiasm is on record and the reason is not. ✅ THE $5,000 CUT IS VERIFIED LIVE AND PUBLIC — the MLS line on all three notices reads $184,000, so the old do-not-quote hedge is retired. 🔴 THE REAL FINDING IS THE OBJECTION AND IT IS VERIFIED THREE WAYS: the problem is SIZE, not price. The clearest read says it in four words — "Just too small." ⛔ NO DISCOUNT REACHES A SIZE OBJECTION. The answer here is AUDIENCE — first-time buyers, downsizers, investors — and a price conversation with this seller would be solving the wrong problem. This board argued for a cut here for weeks on the strength of silence; the showings arrived and said something different, and that earlier read is withdrawn. 🔴 That Saturday burst has now fully decayed with the one phone call still unmade.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $599K package — the plat exists, and the septic answer has been sitting unread for four days
listings.note: ✅ THE DELIVERABLE WAS LOCATED FRIDAY MORNING — the 19-lot plat, which is precisely what the open buyer chip had been waiting on since he answered "Yes". That call stops being a holding reply and becomes a delivery. 🔴 THE THING THAT SHOULD BOTHER YOU MOST ON THIS FILE IS NOT THE COUNTY, IT IS THE HANDOFF: the builder asked the septic perc question on 8/12, your operations manager researched and answered it completely, and that answer has been sitting on her board since Friday with nobody reading it back to him. Day four. The work was done; the delivery never happened. ⭐ THE PERC QUESTION ITSELF IS PRICED RATHER THAN BLOCKED: the county takes record searches in person only, weekdays 8:00 to 3:30, at a per-record fee — across nineteen lots that is a four-figure errand. ⭐ SO THE CHOICE IS THREE-WAY, NOT TWO: send someone for all nineteen, narrow the pull to the lots a buyer is actually asking about, or try the free path first and ask the developer, who almost certainly already holds the perc results from platting. ⭐ PERC DECIDES BUILDABILITY AND BUILDABILITY DECIDES PRICE PER LOT, which is why this one question governs the whole package. 🔥 SIX NAMES OFF THIS AD NOW, while every other ad in the portfolio produced zero. ⚠️ Two builder outreach addresses hard-bounced permanently after 48 hours of retries — part of the builder audience received nothing at all, and those two need replacing rather than resending.

listings.status: 🔴 Active — sixteen days quiet, and the good news is STILL undelivered
listings.note: 🔴 TWO TOURS IN FIVE DAYS AT THE END OF JULY, THEN NOTHING SINCE. On a listing that had gone 126 days with essentially no traffic, that brief burst was the only real activity this file has produced and it has fully decayed. ⭐ THE GOOD NEWS IS STILL UNDELIVERED AT SIXTEEN DAYS, WHICH MAKES IT THE OLDEST OWED ITEM ON THE BOARD: the 7/31 read came back interested No, but with the price called JUST RIGHT, a 4 of 5 rating, and the comment that the buyers prefer the east end of the beach although they liked this complex. That is a GEOGRAPHY loss, not a price loss, and it is the only independent validation of this list price the file has ever carried. ⭐ He is out of state and lives on these reads — lead with the price answer, not the no. ⚠️ A price discrepancy opened during the dark window and is still unresolved: two sources five thousand apart, and neither is quotable until the MLS is read directly.

listings.status: ⚠️ Active $1.15M — biggest listing in the book, seller identity STILL unverified
listings.note: ⚠️ THE LARGEST NUMBER ON YOUR BOARD IS STILL THE ONE WITH THE WEAKEST FILE. No showing, no feedback and no correspondence has crossed this desk on this address in the fourteen-day window. ⛔ THE CLIENT IDENTITY REMAINS UNVERIFIED under the identity law — a name is carried in memory, and memory is not a receipt. On a $1.15M listing that is not a formality: it gates every piece of client-facing creative and every seller email. ⭐ THE POSITIONING READ IS STILL THE MOST USEFUL THING ON THE FILE: the only tour this listing ever took said, verbatim, that the buyer liked the house but the land wasn't what he was looking for. The objection is ACREAGE — which at this price point is the cheapest possible loss, because nobody has ever said it is too expensive. ⭐ THE UNANSWERED QUESTION IS THEREFORE A TARGETING ONE: who is the buyer who wants THIS land, and is the marketing pointed at them. ⏰ The 8/2 open house was never debriefed and its sign-in sheet was never captured — two weeks on, that is effectively lost. 🛑 The lookalike meeting link on this address is still not to be opened, on any device.

listings.status: ⚠️ Active — price cut to $285K on 8/11, and the live ad still shows the old number
listings.note: ⚠️ A PRICE CUT THAT THE MARKETING NEVER HEARD ABOUT, NOW ON DAY SIX. The listing came down to $285,000 on 8/11 per the CRM's own field, while an 8/8 social post that is still live carries $289,900. ⭐ THAT IS A CHEAP FIX AND A REAL ONE — a public ad quoting a dead number is the kind of small inconsistency buyers and agents actually notice, and it makes every other number you publish slightly less trustworthy. ⚠️ IT IS ALSO NOT THE ONLY ONE: Ridge Trail has the identical problem, four days running. Two live ads quoting two dead prices is no longer a one-off, it is a publishing gap. ⚠️ THIS IS TWO ARTIFACTS RATHER THAN TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES, so it is printed as a waiting-on-you item rather than a red flag: the CRM field and the live post disagree, and the MLS has not been read directly to break the tie. ⭐ The corrected creative has been staged for approval since Wednesday, which makes the whole item one click rather than a project.

listings.status: 🔴 Active — the tenant answer is twenty-three days owed
listings.note: 🔴 THE LONGEST-RUNNING BROKEN PROMISE ON THE BOARD, AND IT FINALLY BROKE HER PATIENCE. She left a twenty-two-second voicemail on 7/25 rather than sending a seventh text — which is what a patient client does when nothing comes back — and then on Wednesday night she escalated THREE TIMES IN TWENTY-SEVEN MINUTES: two voicemails and a text. ✅ THE EMERGENCY HALF RESOLVED WITHOUT YOU — power is back on at the property and the tenant paid his balance, both confirmed this week. ⭐ THE OWED THING IS STILL YOURS: she asked whether the tenant on this unit is out, because he owes another month's rent if he isn't. ⚠️ YOU DO NOT NEED AN ANSWER TO MAKE THIS CALL. "Still no word from him, here's exactly what I'm doing about it" beats a twenty-fourth day of silence. ⭐ She is not a loose end — she closed with you in June, still opens your market reports, and has an unclosed valuation loop on this same address.

listings.status: 🆕 Buyer-side pending — long fuse, one answer owed
listings.note: 🆕 REAL GCI THE FORECAST COULD NOT SEE UNTIL LAST WEEK — roughly $44.6K across this address and a second buyer-side file, both weighted at zero in every prior model. That is not new business; it is business you already had that the system was blind to. ⭐ ONE LIVE OPEN ITEM AND IT IS NOW MORE THAN TWO WEEKS OLD: a builder change-order and pre-qualification message, deliberately left in the inbox rather than filed because it is the only thing on this file that wants an answer. ⚠️ Long fuse — it closes late January 2027 with a production builder — so the change order is the only item carrying urgency, and two weeks of silence on a builder question is how change orders get decided without you.

listings.status: 🔴 Buyer-side $2.35M — the counter has never been put on paper, day 26
listings.note: 🔴 THE LARGEST SINGLE NUMBER ON YOUR BOARD, ROUGHLY $36K OF GCI, AND THE WHOLE COST OF MOVING IT IS TWENTY MINUTES OF WRITING. The listing side has asked repeatedly since 7/21 to be moved forward and has never received a written position from your side. ⚠️ STATED HONESTLY: a phone call leaves no receipt, so this is ABSENCE rather than proven failure — but what was promised was paper, and there is none on any lane this desk can read. ⭐ WHY IT KEEPS RETURNING: a seller who reverse-offers a buyer is a seller who wants a deal, and the honest answer IS the counter. Sending it is not a favour to them; it is your position on the record. ⚠️ NOT ASSERTED, AND THIS MATTERS BEFORE ANYTHING GOES OVER: the appraisal figure your buyer cited as far under ask is single-sourced from him. Whose appraisal it is, when it was done, and whether it is a formal appraisal at all are all unknown. Do not quote it to the other side as an appraised value. ⚠️ Three feedback requests from the listing side also remain unanswered.

listings.status: 🎉 Closed + funded — and the referral window on both is wide open
listings.note: ⏰ THE POST-CLOSE REVIEW-ASK ON LAKE FOREST IS NOW TWENTY-SIX DAYS OPEN. On a board where the large majority of this year's closings came from relationships rather than ads, and which needs roughly two contracts a week to reach the goal, this is the single cheapest referral at-bat available and it has sat untouched for nearly four weeks. The gratitude call queued a month ago still has not happened. ⚠️ One open courtesy: the other office still owes those sellers the deed for utilities. 🎯 WHISPERING PINES IS STILL THE ONE UNRESOLVED UNIT IN THE COUNT, and it is worth a number: settling the agent-of-record in your favour makes the year 23 instead of 22 and moves pace by nearly two full closings.
